attempt: Rely on PNG alpha and BlockType.RequiresAlphaBlending without marking the model's glazing face transparent
reason_failed: User reported opaque glass in the Hytale client although Blockbench looked transparent. Direct inspection found CubeFace.transparent=false; the exported face lacked the new native transparent flag.
error_signature: Glass texture alpha=90/255, block blending=true, but glazing textureLayout.front.transparent absent
conditions: Editor preview honors alpha differently from the game's per-face rendering pass
Composite model requires only the pane, not opaque masonry, to participate in transparent-face rendering
workaround: Set transparent on the actual glazing face through Blockbench and verify the native codec exports textureLayout.front.transparent=true. Retain block alpha blending and PNG alpha. Native data tests passed after change; corrected client output still awaiting user review.

source_refs.description: Previous exported pane lacked the face flag
Re-export from actual Blockbench includes flag only for pane
Primary Hytale notes introduce model face transparency and per-block alpha blending
